title: Macro Defect Inspection - Contamination Detection on Candela 8520
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 5nm Node Manufacturing
author: James Rodriguez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Candela 8520 system to detect and classify Contamination defects during post-cmp inspection at the 5nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Contamination defects that are critical to yield at the 5nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Candela 8520 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Candela 8520
- Inspection Type: Macro Defect Inspection
- Target Defect: Contamination
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 5nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all Candela 8520 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for post-cmp monitoring in the 5nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Candela 8520
Software Version: v13.6.758
Recipe: MACRO_DEFECT_INSPECTION_5nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (122 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Candela 8520 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Macro Defect Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Contamination defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 5nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 76 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.7% for Macro Defect Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-11-05
Wafers Tested: 31
Total Defects Found: 1619
Defect Density: 515.34 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.1%
Capture Rate: 97.4%
Test Duration: 259 minutes
System Uptime: 98.8%

Result Classification: NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Candela 8520 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Contamination at the 5nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) No significant drift was observed during the test duration.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
